overall: Atlanta is starting the day warm but calm at 73.4°F with near-zero warming velocity as of 05:49 ET — temps have been essentially flat overnight. The day is poised for a significant rise into the low 90s before afternoon convection (60% PoP, likely thunderstorms) introduces meaningful uncertainty about whether the peak gets cut short. A Heat Advisory is in effect with heat index values up to 106°F, underscoring how humid and primed for heat the airmass is.
forecast_obs_notes: Models are modestly spread: GFS runs hot at 93.4°F while HRRR and NBM cluster near 87.1–87.3°F, reflecting storm-cooling scenarios; ECMWF splits the difference at 90.1°F. The NWS narrative explicitly calls for a high near 91°F but notes temperatures falling to around 87°F in the afternoon — a strong signal that convective activity is expected to truncate the peak before it can hold at the day's maximum reading, pulling some model guidance lower.
max_temp_prediction: The META model (most reliable fused output) places highest probability on 90–91°F (36.1%) followed closely by 92–93°F (33.9%), consistent with the NWS call of near 91°F. The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets, where the top bucket is 87–88°F at just 21.1% — but the ensemble flags this as Tier 4 / no_trade, and the broader probability distribution strongly favors the 90–93°F range. Confidence is moderate: afternoon storm timing is the key wildcard, as an early storm could clip the high into the upper 80s, while a delayed or weaker convective event would allow temps to reach the low 90s.
